By  Devanshi Basu

State-level approval map 18 months into President Donald Trump‘s second term reveals that his political footing has slipped significantly since his return to the White House. A new Civiqs analysis tracking 117,851 registered voters shows once-reliable territory now looking far less certain, raising questions for Republicans ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.

results.content: Trump entered his second term with positive approval ratings in every state he had won by double digits. Since then, however, his standing has steadily weakened. According to the Civiqs data, his approval rating turned negative in some Republican states after he announced tariffs on U.S. trading partners in April. In Kentucky and Missouri, the shift into negative territory occurred after the Trump administration announced military action against Iran in February.

Since late May, Trump's net approval, the difference between approval and disapproval ratings, has remained around 4%, down from 7% in early May. Most recently, 50% of Tennessee residents approve of his performance, 44% disapprove, and 6% are neutral.

Trump's net approval in Tennessee began at 24% when he took office, declined to 7% by late 2025, and has not risen above 5% since May 5. During his first term, he started with a 17% net rating and ended with an 11% rating.
